Hana V.: Quick one 5252 team taxi from hotel to venue yesterday. Corp card paid a single charge of $92.40 but Maya paid me $20 cash for her share at pickup. Need to split the corp-card line: business portion $60.40, personal tip $12, and Maya's $20 was covered in cash. How do I submit so corp ledger is correct and Maya isn't double-reimbursed?
Maya A.: Confirmed I gave Hana $20 cash. I paid because my phone had no signal to Venmo.
expense-bot: To split a corp-card transaction use two lines and attach proof. Example:
```
/expenses submit --card-split
line1: 60.40 USD -> business - taxi to conference, attach taxi_receipt.jpg
line2: 12.00 USD -> personal - tip
notes: "Team taxi 2026-02-10. Maya paid $20 cash to Hana at pickup; include cash receipt or sign-off."
```
Hana V.: Uploaded taxi_receipt.jpg -> https://redwood-files/receipts/taxi_1918004444.jpg ; photo_of_cash-note.jpg -> https://redwood-files/receipts/cashnote_1918004444.jpg
Kira (Finance): Thanks @Hana. A few things: 1) We need the taxi receipt itemized to confirm fare vs tip (your photo looks like it shows both). 2) For cash reimbursements between employees, we require a confirmation from the person who paid (Maya) in the thread or a signed cash acknowledgement. 3) Finance will reimburse the business portion to the corporate ledger and create a personal-charge for the tip if you ask us to bill you. Alternatively, you can pay the tip personally to avoid a payroll deduction.
Hana V.: The receipt is itemized: fare $72.40, tip $12.00, total $84.40. The corp card shows $92.40 because there was an extra service fee the vendor added later ($8.00). So math: fare $72.40 - Maya $20 cash = $52.40 business on corp card, plus service fee $8 = $60.40 business, tip $12 personal. Does that work?
Luis M.: Approving manager sign-off for the business portion and the cash split. Hana, confirm Maya's cash payment here please.
Maya A.: Confirmed I paid Hana $20 cash at pickup. Happy to confirm for finance.
Kira (Finance): OK good. We'll accept the cash confirmation in-thread. Please do the /expenses submit with two lines: business $60.40 (attach receipt) and personal tip $12.00. Add a note: "Maya paid $20 cash; see thread confirmation." Finance will reimburse the $60.40 to the corporate ledger and create a $12.00 personal charge if you don't want to pay it personally. For the $8 vendor service fee we've classified that as allowable incidental and will include in the business portion since it's under our $10 per-incident threshold.
Hana V.: Submitted with notes and attachments, tagged @Kira and @Luis.
